title: Tenant-aware shadow traffic slice and graceful degradation runbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Provide an operational playbook for performing a tenant-aware partial traffic shift using a shadow traffic slice plus controlled graceful degradation during cross-region disruptions. This runbook is intended for both Hosted and Dedicated deployments and focuses on minimizing customer-visible errors by: 1) exercising a low-percentage shadow slice to validate downstream compatibility, 2) applying tenant-prioritized adaptive shaping and soft rate-caps, and 3) coordinating KV cache resynchronization and leader-election-sensitive services. The document contains pre-checks, step-by-step execution instructions, emergency rollback steps, communication templates, and post-incident actions. This ticket will produce a single canonical runbook doc, a CLI-helper script (infra PR), and a communication package for CSMs and support.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc created and reviewed by oncall & reliability (>=2 reviewers)
Automated CLI helper for creating a shadow traffic slice validated in staging (integration tests passing)
Playbook tested in a scheduled chaos window with <10% error delta for VIP tenants and documented results
Customer comms templates approved by Support and Legal
Metrics and dashboards (traffic-slice, tenant-error-rate, kv-desync) added to out-of-box incident dashboard
runbook_steps: 1) Pre-checks (owner: oncall): verify regional health markers: region-ctl.p95-latency < 300ms, region-util < 80%, KV-leader-count stable. Ensure backup control-plane reachable.
2) Identify candidate tenants: run tenant-priority query (VIP > SLA > Standard > Free). Record tenant IDs and current thresholds in incident ticket.
3) Create a shadow-slice config at 1% traffic using routing-layer feature flag 'shadow-slice:tenant-aware' and route to alternate-region pool. Validate successful 200 OKs for health probes for 60s.
4) Observe key signals for 5 minutes: per-tenant token generation success, KV cache hit-rate, per-tenant latencies. If error rate > 1% for VIPs, abort and notify SRE lead.
5) Increment shadow slice to 5% for non-VIP tenants only, while keeping VIPs at 100% local until compatibility confirmed.
6) If shadow traffic is stable, enable adaptive request shaping for non-critical tenants: apply soft rate caps (1.25x normal) and enable backlog-shed policy for burst paths.
7) For Dedicated customers with reserved pools: coordinate with account owner to apply 'dedicated-burst' policy; do not move tenant stateful lanes without express permission.
8) KV cache resync: for cross-region failover, run kv-sync probe; if mismatch > 0.5% keys for any tenant, schedule targeted resync (see kv-resync playbook link).
9) Circuit markers: toggle tenant-circuit:degraded for low-priority tenants to avoid downstream timeouts; allow degraded responses with structured meta explaining partial results.

10) Monitor for 30 minutes. If overall error budget remains < 10% of baseline for VIPs and non-VIP degradation pattern matches expected, proceed to phased traffic shift (10% increments every 5 minutes for non-VIP tenants).
11) Full traffic shift plan (only if stability criteria met): move 50% non-VIP traffic, validate, then 100% for non-VIP. VIPs should only be moved after explicit product/SRE sign-off.
12) Post-shift stabilization: run 'kv-heal' for any tombstoned entries and monitor consistency windows for 24 hours. Keep shadow-slice active for 1 hour as safety net.
13) Communication: trigger internal incident channel and customer notifications per template. Update stakeholders every 15 minutes while active.
14) Finalize: document actions, timestamps, and metrics in incident artifact and schedule postmortem within 72 hours.
Safety guardrails: abort and rollback immediately on any: sustained VIP error rate increase > 0.5%, control-plane errors, or detection of KV divergence > 2% for VIP tenants.
rollback_steps: A) Immediate: flip routing flag to previous stable config (toggle 'shadow-slice' off) and route all traffic back to originating region pool.
B) Revert adaptive shaping and remove tenant-circuit:degraded markers; restore original rate-limits from saved snapshot.
C) If KV cache was mutated during shift, mark affected tenants as 'state-verify' and run targeted checkpoint restore from snapshot taken in step 0. Document any data loss risk and notify customers.
D) For Dedicated: coordinate with account operations to restore dedicated pool allocation and run acceptance test suite on customer traffic lanes.
E) Post-rollback: collect diagnostics (heap, kernel traces, leader logs) and attach to incident ticket for debug.
tenant_prioritization_matrix: VIP: strict SLA, no silent degradation; require manual approval to shift; primary recovery path should preserve consistency.
SLA: allowed controlled degradation with customer notice; prefer shadow-validate then gradual shift.
Standard: soft caps and structured degrade allowed; move early in shift plan.
Free/Tiered trial: lowest priority for resources; consider circuit-shed early to protect VIPs.
dedicated_vs_hosted_notes: Hosted: have fallbacks to compatible model-variants; automated routing policies can be applied globally by platform oncall.
Dedicated: tenant pools may be physically isolated. Obtain account ops approval before any cross-pool movement. For Dedicated, prefer read-only shadow validation approaches to avoid state mutation.
Private/VPC: runbook contains operator notes but final migration steps require customer operator participation and a signed runbook handoff.
observability_playbook: Add temporary widgets: tenant_error_rate_by_priority, shadow_slice_success_rate, kv_key_delta_by_tenant.
Set alerts: VIP_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> pager SRE-lead; shadow_probe_fail > 3 -> notify oncall.
Trace sampling: increase trace capture to 100% for impacted tenants for 10 minutes after a shift to gather stack traces and latency hotspots.
comms_templates: Internal status (15m cadence): [INC-ENG-<id>] Active cross-region mitigation. Shadow-slice at X%. Observed VIP errors: Y%. Next step: Z. Owner: <oncall>.

Customer template (initial): We are currently routing a small percentage of requests across regions to mitigate degraded performance in <region>. No action required; you may observe slightly higher latencies for non-critical requests. We will notify you if your traffic is affected.

Customer template (escalation): Your account (tenant <id>) is being prioritized for recovery. We have applied temporary safeguards and will follow up with detailed post-incident notes within 72 hours.
